_comment: Fragment 29 — D-72, G65 and G66 closed; two checks installed, G65 narrowed. Merged 2026-08-21.

nodes.label: D-72 — G65 and G66 Closed, C-14 Now Six Checks
nodes.description: Two checks installed under a guardrail lifted for these items only. scripts/checks/settings-parse.mjs parse-checks the repo-local settings cascade; scripts/checks/decision-status.mjs cross-references decision status between the register and Modular_PRD section 10 in both directions. Five of the six checks run in CI; graph coverage stays local-only.
nodes.rationale: Both gaps were opened by D-71 as the parent defects behind six stale claims. Closing them converts two manual review habits into controls, and the decision-status check found a live defect on its first run.

nodes.label: G65 Closed on a Narrower Promise Than It Opened With
nodes.description: G65 asked for a check verifying that a tier is correct rather than that a decision merely arrived there. A script cannot semantically validate prose, so that framing is not buildable. What was built instead is a bidirectional cross-reference of decision status between the register and Modular_PRD section 10. The tier sweep still verifies arrival, not correctness.
nodes.rationale: Recorded as a scope reduction rather than delivered quietly as though it were the original ask. A gap closed against a narrower remedy without saying so is exactly the defect G25 turned out to be, where two of three named targets were done and the closure text named only the two.

nodes.label: The Same-Commit Design Was Tested and Rejected
nodes.description: The intuitive design for G65 was to verify a tier claim against git: did the commit that recorded the decision also touch the claimed tier file? Tested against both observed defects, it catches neither. D-70's commit did touch the artifact inventory — it flipped three rows, and the defect was a fourth it missed — and D-57's did touch Modular_PRD. Both would pass.
nodes.rationale: Recorded because the design is appealing, cheap, and wrong, so a later reader will likely propose it again. Testing a proposed control against the defects it is meant to catch, before building it, is the same discipline that dissolved the ESLint preset question and withdrew G64's inference limb.

nodes.label: Q10 Was Missing From the List of What the Chief Editor Owes
nodes.description: The decision-status check's first live catch. Q1, Q7 and Q10 were Open and Chief-Editor-owned in Modular_PRD section 10 but absent from section 5.1's outstanding-decisions list. Q10 is the named blocker for Stage D, cited repeatedly in D-70 as the reason migration 0002 cannot be written, and it was missing from the one line a decision-maker reads to know what is outstanding.
nodes.rationale: The list was wrong in both directions: D-71 removed four items already decided, and this adds three never listed. Owner is load-bearing — Q9 is Open but owned by the customer via the sponsor, so its absence from a list of Chief Editor decisions is correct, and the check excludes it. The three are now visible, not answered; Q10 still blocks Stage D.

nodes.label: What the New Checks Still Cannot See
nodes.description: The decision-status check compares status labels, not the substance behind them — it cannot tell whether a decision was correctly decided, only whether the two records agree. The QA3, QB, QD and QE series has no Modular_PRD section 10 row, so the open-but-unlisted direction cannot see those four at all; they rest on manual review.
nodes.rationale: Stated so coverage is not overread, in the same shape as C-14's local-only limitation. A control whose blind spots are unstated invites the belief that everything it does not report is fine.
